mainTopic: בית שמאי's reasoning about an עם הארץ's vessels and טומאת מת, when an עם הארץ is trusted about immersion, and the משנה's extra stringencies for קודש over תרומה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing בית שמאי's reasoning: the עם הארץ's food and earthenware vessels are called pure only for his own sake, but vessels a חבר might borrow are not. רבי יהושע objects sharply, and a student of בית שמאי explains their reason. An impure vessel cannot block טומאה, and an עם הארץ would never listen if told his vessel is impure. רבי יהושע then apologizes at the graves of בית שמאי and fasts for the rest of his life. Back in the main discussion, the גמרא explains that a חבר immerses whatever he borrows, but that does not help for טומאת מת, which takes seven days to remove. It then asks when an עם הארץ is trusted about טבילה, with answers from אביי (body versus vessels, with trust only at the end of the process) and רבא (a simple denial versus a technical claim). Next the גמרא explains the משנה's terms 'back and inside' and בית הצביטה. It discusses רב ביבי's ברייתא and רבה בר אבוה's teaching that six of the eleven stringencies apply to חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש. Finally it starts explaining why one carrying a מדרס may not carry קודש, through a story told by שמואל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The purity is only for the עם הארץ himself
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי's reasoning: food and earthenware vessels are declared pure only for the עם הארץ, because a חבר never uses them. But a vessel that a חבר might also use is not declared pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only called it pure for him himself. But should we call a vessel pure when its purity matters both to you and to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why בית שמאי treat food and earthenware vessels differently from metal vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חבר never treats the food or earthenware vessels of an עם הארץ as pure, so calling them 'pure' harms nobody. A metal vessel is different. A חבר might borrow it and only immerse it, not knowing it needs full purification from טומאת מת. So בית שמאי will not call that kind of vessel pure.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person who is not careful about the laws of purity
Someone who has committed to keeping the laws of purity carefully

steps.confusionAlert: 'We declared it pure' does not mean the item is truly pure for everyone. It means the item is treated as pure only for the עם הארץ's own use.

phrases.english: We declared it pure for him himself.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the עם הארץ, the owner of the food and earthenware vessels.

phrases.english: But shall we declare pure the vessel,
whose purity is for you and for him?
phrases.notes: 'You' is the חבר, who might one day borrow this vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעַצְמוֹ טִהַרְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of בית שמאי's reason, which began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do בית שמאי protect food and earthenware vessels but not metal vessels?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'purity' only matters to the עם הארץ himself. Vessels a חבר might use are not declared pure.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the woman is impure but her dough is pure?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע attacks בית שמאי's view with two strange results: an impure woman and bowl with pure dough, and an impure pitcher with pure liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע said, 'I am ashamed of your words, בית שמאי! Can it be that a woman kneads dough in a bowl, the woman and the bowl are impure for seven days, and the dough is pure? Or a pitcher full of liquid, the pitcher is impure for seven days, and the liquid is pure?!'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבי יהושע's challenge. He argues that בית שמאי's rule leads to results that make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under בית שמאי, the metal bowl and pitcher are not protected, so they become impure for seven days. Yet the dough and liquid inside them are protected and stay pure. רבי יהושע finds it absurd that the container is impure while what sits inside it is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Seven-day impurity, the impurity that comes from a dead body

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
I am ashamed of your words, Beit Shammai!
Is it possible that a woman kneads in a bowl,
the woman and the bowl are impure for seven days,
and the dough is pure?
A pitcher full of liquids,
the pitcher is impure with seven-day impurity,
and the liquids are pure?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹשַׁנִי מִדִּבְרֵיכֶם, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of בית שמאי explained in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's split between food and earthenware vessels, which are protected, and metal vessels, which are not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is unreasonable for a container to be impure while the food or liquid inside it stays pure.

steps.title: A student offers to explain בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: A student of בית שמאי comes over to רבי יהושע and offers to explain their reason. רבי יהושע tells him to go ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the students of בית שמאי joined him and said, 'I will tell you the reason of בית שמאי.' He said to him, 'Speak.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing a defense of בית שמאי against רבי יהושע's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled on yet. The student will answer through a series of questions, getting רבי יהושע to agree to each point one step at a time.

phrases.english: One student approached him
from among the students of Beit Shammai,
he said to him: I will tell you
the reasoning of Beit Shammai.
He said to him: Speak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמַר לְךָ טַעְמָן שֶׁל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the response to רבי יהושע's challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This line introduces the defense of בית שמאי.

steps.title: Does an impure vessel block impurity?
steps.stepSummary: The student asks whether an impure vessel acts as a barrier against טומאת מת. רבי יהושע answers that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him, 'Does an impure vessel act as a barrier or not?' He answered, 'It does not act as a barrier.'
steps.whatsHappening: The student gets רבי יהושע to agree to the first building block of his argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a pure vessel can block impurity from spreading. An impure vessel offers no protection at all.

phrases.english: He said to him: An impure vessel,
does it act as a barrier or not?
He said to him: It does not act as a barrier.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלִי טָמֵא חוֹצֵץ אוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First point in the student's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can an impure vessel block טומאת מת?

steps.title: An עם הארץ's vessel counts as impure
steps.stepSummary: The student asks whether an עם הארץ's vessel is pure or impure. רבי יהושע answers that it is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Is a vessel of an עם הארץ pure or impure?' He answered, 'Impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The student gets רבי יהושע to agree to a second point. Put together with step 4, it leads to a surprising result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ's vessel counts as impure, and an impure vessel cannot block. So by strict law, his earthenware vessel should protect nothing, and everything in the room should be impure. That means the 'protection' בית שמאי give to food and earthenware vessels was never real purity in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel belonging to an עם הארץ

phrases.english: A vessel of an am ha'aretz,
is it impure or pure?
He said to him: Impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלִי שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ טָמֵא אוֹ טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second point, building on step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of an עם הארץ's vessel?

steps.title: He won't listen anyway, so we call it pure for him
steps.stepSummary: Telling the עם הארץ that his vessel is impure accomplishes nothing, since he would ignore it or even turn it around on you. So בית שמאי treat it as pure for his own sake only.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If you tell him it is impure, will he pay any attention to you? And not only that: if you tell him it is impure, he will answer you, "Mine is pure and yours is impure."'
steps.whatsHappening: The student finishes his answer to רבי יהושע. The 'pure' dough was only ever a concession to an עם הארץ who would not listen anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Really, everything in the room is impure, because the עם הארץ's vessel cannot block. But since he would ignore a ruling of impurity, there is no point telling him that his own food and earthenware vessels are impure. A חבר never uses those items anyway. So the result רבי יהושע called absurd is not a claim of true purity. It just reflects what is worth telling the עם הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Mine is pure and yours is impure

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's 'pure' food and earthenware vessels are only pure for the עם הארץ himself, since he would never accept being told otherwise. Metal vessels, which a חבר might borrow, are treated as truly impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רבי יהושע's challenge. The odd split between the bowl and the dough is not a statement about real purity. It is a practical choice about what to tell someone who will not listen.

phrases.english: And if you tell him "impure,"
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the עם הארץ who owns the vessel.

phrases.english: does he pay any attention to you?
And not only that, but
if you tell him "impure,"
he says to you: "Mine is pure and yours is impure."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לוֹ טָמֵא, כְּלוּם מַשְׁגִּיחַ עָלֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from steps 4 and 5 to answer the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the purity בית שמאי grant as a practical concession rather than true purity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע assumed בית שמאי hold that the dough is truly pure while its bowl is impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: By strict law, everything in the room is impure. The dough is only called 'pure' for the עם הארץ, since telling him otherwise would be pointless.

steps.title: This is the reason of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The student wraps up his explanation and says this is the reasoning behind בית שמאי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is the reason of בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The student of בית שמאי closes his explanation. He tells רבי יהושע that what he just laid out is בית שמאי's full reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food, drink and clay vessels of an עם הארץ are treated as pure 'for him' because a חבר would not use them anyway. Metal vessels might one day be borrowed by a חבר, so בית שמאי call them impure. With that, the strange results from רבי יהושע's attack now make sense.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's ruling is not about how impurity physically works. It is a practical step: they treat things as pure only where it affects the עם הארץ alone.

phrases.english: And that is the reason of Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזֶהוּ טַעְמָן שֶׁל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the student's explanation from step 6
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בית שמאי's ruling is fully explained by the practical concern about the עם הארץ's vessels.

steps.title: רבי יהושע apologizes at the graves of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע lies down on the graves of בית שמאי. He humbles himself and praises even their unexplained rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away רבי יהושע went and lay down on the graves of בית שמאי. He said: I humble myself before you, bones of בית שמאי! If your unexplained teachings are this wise, your explained teachings must be wiser still.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a story. רבי יהושע regrets his earlier sharp words against בית שמאי, so he goes to their graves to apologize.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יהושע had said he was embarrassed by בית שמאי's words. Now he sees their ruling was wise all along. He reasons with a קל וחומר: if their unexplained rulings make this much sense, their explained ones surely do.

phrases.english: Immediately Rabbi Yehoshua went
and lay prostrate on the graves of Beit Shammai,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: נַעֲנֵיתִי לָכֶם עַצְמוֹת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי!
phrases.english: he said: I humble myself before you, bones of Beit Shammai!
If your unexplained rulings are like this,
your explained ones, all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד הָלַךְ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְנִשְׁתַּטַּח עַל קִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaction to hearing בית שמאי's reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע admits בית שמאי were right and humbles himself before them.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's teeth darkened from fasting
steps.stepSummary: People reported that רבי יהושע fasted so much for his words against בית שמאי that his teeth turned dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: People said: all his life his teeth were darkened because of his fasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a report about רבי יהושע. He fasted for the rest of his life, and his teeth turned dark from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how seriously he took speaking wrongly about other Torah scholars. The fasts were to make up for his earlier words against בית שמאי.

phrases.english: They said: all his days
his teeth were blackened because of his fasts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ כׇּל יָמָיו הוּשְׁחֲרוּ שִׁינָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע fasted all his life for his words against בית שמאי.

steps.title: The teaching shows we borrow vessels from an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its main topic. The words 'for you and for him' prove that חברים borrow vessels from עמי הארץ. That raises a worry about improperly immersed vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyway, the teaching says 'for you and for him.' So it seems we do borrow from them!
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא goes back to the question it was working on. It points out that this teaching assumes a חבר borrows vessels from an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vessel's status matters 'for you' (the חבר) too, then a חבר must sometimes use the עם הארץ's vessels. That brings back the earlier worry: maybe the עם הארץ immersed them the wrong way, so they are still impure when the חבר borrows them.
steps.confusionAlert: Here שאל means 'borrow,' not 'ask a question.'

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches "for you and for him,"
phrases.notes: This points back to the words 'שטהרתו לך ולו' in step 1: the vessel's status matters both to the חבר and to the עם הארץ.

phrases.english: apparently we borrow from them!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת לְךָ וָלוֹ אַלְמָא שָׁאֲלִינַן מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the main question about borrowing from an עם הארץ
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that we need not worry about how an עם הארץ immerses his vessels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If חברים borrow vessels from עמי הארץ, an improperly immersed vessel could reach the חבר while still impure.

steps.title: We immerse what we borrow
steps.stepSummary: There is no problem, because a חבר immerses any vessel he borrows from an עם הארץ before using it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we borrow from them, we immerse the vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry. The חבר does his own טבילה on whatever he borrows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חבר purifies the vessel himself, it does not matter whether the עם הארץ immersed it properly. The borrowing is safe.

phrases.english: When we borrow from them, we immerse them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי שָׁיְילִינַן מִינַּיְיהוּ מַטְבְּלִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry raised in step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution: the borrower purifies the vessel himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Borrowing from an עם הארץ risks using a vessel that is still impure
steps.terutzMaskana: The חבר immerses borrowed vessels, so earlier mistakes do not matter

steps.title: Then בית הלל should answer בית שמאי the same way
steps.stepSummary: If immersing borrowed vessels solves the problem, בית הלל could have told בית שמאי the same thing. Then metal vessels would not need to be called impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let בית הלל answer בית שמאי: when we borrow from them, we immerse them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from step 11 against בית שמאי's own reason. If immersing works, why did בית שמאי worry about a חבר borrowing metal vessels?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי called the עם הארץ's metal vessels impure because a חבר might borrow them. But if the חבר immerses anything he borrows, that worry disappears. Then בית הלל's view, that everything stays pure, should win easily.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, נַיהְדְּרוּ לְהוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: If so, let Beit Hillel reply to Beit Shammai:
When we borrow from them, we immerse them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי נַיהְדְּרוּ לְהוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 11 to challenge בית שמאי's reason from step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's reason for calling the עם הארץ's metal vessels impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the borrower always immerses, the fear that a חבר will borrow an impure vessel is gone.

steps.title: Corpse impurity needs seven days, and no one lends that long
steps.stepSummary: The case is about טומאת מת. That needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days, and people do not lend vessels for seven days. So the borrower cannot purify the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something impure from a corpse needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days, and people do not lend a vessel for seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why immersing does not help in this case. Purifying from corpse impurity takes a full week, which is far too long for a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary impurity can be removed with one quick טבילה, so the borrower can handle it. טומאת מת needs הזאה (sprinkling with ashes of the פרה אדומה) on days three and seven. No one lends a vessel for that long, so the borrower cannot purify it. That is why בית שמאי's worry still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: something made impure by a corpse
sprinkling with ashes of the פרה אדומה

steps.whatToRemember: Immersing a borrowed vessel works for ordinary impurity. It does not work for טומאת מת, which takes a week to remove, so בית שמאי's concern stays in place.

phrases.aramaic: טְמֵא מֵת בָּעֵי הַזָּאָה שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי,
phrases.english: Something impure from a corpse requires sprinkling on the third and seventh days,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָנָא לְשִׁבְעָה יוֹמֵי לָא מוֹשְׁלִי אִינָשֵׁי.
phrases.english: and people do not lend a vessel for seven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: טְמֵא מֵת בָּעֵי הַזָּאָה שְׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The borrower's טבילה solves every kind of impurity
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאת מת needs a seven-day process, longer than any loan, so the borrower cannot fix it
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'just immerse it' solution only works for impurities that can be removed quickly.

steps.title: Aren't עמי הארץ trusted about immersion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that an עם הארץ cannot be trusted about טבילה, using a ברייתא that says he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that עמי הארץ are not trusted about immersion? But a ברייתא teaches that עמי הארץ are trusted about the purity of the immersion of someone who became impure from a dead body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions its own last answer. It said a חבר must immerse vessels borrowed from an עם הארץ, but a ברייתא says an עם הארץ is trusted about טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 assumed we cannot rely on an עם הארץ saying, 'I already immersed this.' The ברייתא says we do rely on him for the טבילה of טומאת מת. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in a מקוה to become pure
Someone or something made impure by a dead body

phrases.english: But are they not trusted about immersion?
phrases.notes: "They" means עמי הארץ. This questions the rule that a חבר must re-immerse vessels he borrows.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
עמי הארץ are trusted
regarding the purity of the immersion of one impure from a dead body!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַטְּבִילָה לָא מְהֵימְנִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind Step 11 that an עם הארץ is not trusted about immersion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a חבר must immerse vessels borrowed from an עם הארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says עמי הארץ are trusted about טבילה of טומאת מת, so why not trust them about their vessels?

steps.title: אביי: body versus vessels
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the ברייתא trusts an עם הארץ about immersing his body, but not about immersing his vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no difficulty. This ברייתא is about his body; this rule is about his vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction by splitting the cases. The עם הארץ is believed about his own body, but not about his vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that trusts the עם הארץ speaks about his own טבילה. The rule that a חבר must re-immerse speaks about the עם הארץ's vessels. Since they are different cases, there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: אביי said: It is not difficult:
this is about his body,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא that trusts the עם הארץ.

phrases.english: this is about his vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּגוּפוֹ, הָא בְּכֵלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14 by separating body from vessels.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the עם הארץ is trusted on טבילה, he should be trusted about his vessels too.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is trusted about his own body only, not about his vessels.

steps.title: רבא: simple fact versus technical detail
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sources are about vessels. An עם הארץ is trusted on a simple claim, but not on a detail he may not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both are about his vessels, and there is no difficulty. The ברייתא is where he says, 'I never immersed a vessel inside another vessel.' Our rule is where he says, 'I did immerse one inside another, but never inside a vessel whose opening is narrower than the tube of a wineskin.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the same question. Both sources are about vessels, but the difference is what kind of claim the עם הארץ makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I never put one vessel inside another' is a simple fact, and we believe it. Saying 'I did, but the outer vessel's opening was wide enough' depends on a technical rule an עם הארץ may not know or care about. So we don't trust him on that.

keyTerms.meaning: The tube of a wineskin, a standard minimum width

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about whether an עם הארץ is honest. His point is that an עם הארץ is not careful about fine details, so he can be trusted on a simple 'never did it' but not on 'I did it correctly.'

phrases.english: רבא said: Both this and that are about his vessels,
and it is not difficult:
this is where he said,
"I never immersed a vessel inside a vessel,"
and this is where he said, "I did immerse that way,
but I did not immerse inside a vessel
whose opening is not as wide as the tube of a wineskin."

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּכֵלָיו, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 14 that is different from אביי's answer in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by type of claim (simple fact vs. technical detail)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא trusting עמי הארץ about טבילה seems to contradict the rule that a חבר must re-immerse vessels he borrows from them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about vessels. He is trusted on a simple denial, but not on technical correctness.

steps.title: Support: trusted on 'not made susceptible', not on 'susceptible but not impure'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבא's idea: an עם הארץ is trusted on a simple fact about produce, but not on a detailed claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so a ברייתא teaches: An עם הארץ is trusted to say produce was never made able to become impure. But he is not trusted to say the produce was made able to become impure but did not actually become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same pattern as רבא's answer, as support for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'water never touched this produce' is a simple fact, so he is believed. Saying 'it got wet, but I guarded it from impurity' needs careful watching, which we don't trust him to have done. That is the same line רבא drew for vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: Were made able to become impure (usually by touching water)

steps.whatToRemember: An עם הארץ is trusted on a simple 'it never happened,' but not on 'it happened, and I handled it correctly.'

phrases.english: And so it was taught in a ברייתא:
An עם הארץ is trusted to say
that produce was not made able to become impure,
but he is not trusted to say
that produce was made able to become impure but did not become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: נֶאֱמָן עַם הָאָרֶץ לוֹמַר פֵּירוֹת לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבא's answer in Step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's line between a simple fact and a detailed claim
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about an עם הארץ's claims about produce

steps.title: Is an עם הארץ really trusted about his own body?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: a ברייתא shows an עם הארץ is not trusted about his own purification process.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he really trusted about his body? But a ברייתא teaches: a חבר who comes to be sprinkled is sprinkled right away. An עם הארץ who comes to be sprinkled is not sprinkled until he does the third and seventh days in front of us!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to אביי's answer and attacks it. If an עם הארץ is trusted about his body, why must he count his days in front of us?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the עם הארץ is trusted about his own body. But this ברייתא shows that we do not believe him when he says his days of טומאת מת have passed. The חבר is believed right away, but the עם הארץ is not, which seems to contradict אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: To be sprinkled with מי חטאת (purifying water)
The third and seventh days of purification from טומאת מת

phrases.english: And about his body, is he trusted?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
A חבר who comes to be sprinkled
they sprinkle on him right away,
an עם הארץ who comes to be sprinkled
they do not sprinkle on him
until he does the third and the seventh days in front of us!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַגּוּפוֹ מִי מְהֵימַן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's line and returns to challenge אביי's answer from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that an עם הארץ is trusted about his own body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that an עם הארץ is not believed about his own purification days, so how can we say he is trusted about his body?

steps.title: אביי's new answer: strict at the start, lenient at the end
steps.stepSummary: אביי refines his earlier answer. He still holds that the עם הארץ is trusted about his own body. But he now explains that this trust covers only the immersion at the end of his purification, because we were already strict with him at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: because of the stringency you put on him at his beginning, you are lenient with him at his end.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge in Step 18 by refining his answer. The ברייתא there is about the start of purification, where we are strict, and that strictness is why we can trust the עם הארץ about his body's immersion at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 18 is about the beginning of the process: the עם הארץ must count the third and seventh days in front of us. The ברייתא that trusts him is about the immersion at the end. Since the start was handled strictly, his claim that he immersed his body at the end can be believed. His vessels still need immersing by the borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
At its beginning / at its end

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's view stands: an עם הארץ is trusted about immersing his own body. That trust only covers the end of the process, and it is given because we were strict with him at the start.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Because of the stringency that you applied to him at his beginning,
phrases.notes: 'His beginning' means the start of his purification process.

phrases.english: you are lenient with him at his end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 by separating the beginning of the purification process from its end, which keeps אביי's answer from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the earlier answer: trust about the body applies to the end of the process (immersion), not the beginning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the עם הארץ is not trusted about counting the third and seventh days, he should not be trusted about his body at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is not trusted about the beginning of the process, but because of that strictness he is trusted about the final immersion of his body. His vessels are still not trusted.

steps.title: What does 'the back and the inside' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks what it means by 'the back and the inside' of a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'the back and the inside.' What does 'the back and the inside' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list of laws where קודש is stricter than תרומה. It quotes the phrase 'the back and the inside' and asks what it means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only mentions this law in a few words. The גמרא wants to know which rule about a vessel's back and inside the משנה is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: The back or outside of a vessel
What is? What does it mean?

phrases.english: "The back and the inside."
phrases.notes: These words are quoted from the משנה, which lists this law as applying to תרומה but not to קודש.

phrases.english: What is "the back and the inside"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עם הארץ discussion and returns to explain a new item in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law is meant by the משנה's phrase 'the back and the inside'?

steps.title: A vessel's back can become impure without its inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if only the back of a vessel became impure through liquids, only the back is impure. If the inside became impure, the whole vessel is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if the back of a vessel became impure through liquids, its back is impure, but its inside, rim, ear-handle and handles are pure. If its inside became impure, all of it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a משנה about vessels. When impure liquid touches only the outside of a vessel, only the outside becomes impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity from liquids touching the outside affects only the outside. The other parts of the vessel stay pure. But impurity on the inside makes the whole vessel impure. Our משנה teaches that this split only works for תרומה. For קודש, there is no split.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה counts 'back and inside' as a place where קודש is stricter. With תרומה we split the vessel into parts, but with קודש we do not.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מסכת כלים.

phrases.english: A vessel whose back became impure through liquids:
its back is impure,
its inside, its rim, its ear-shaped handle, and its handles are pure.
If its inside became impure, all of it is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The back and the inside' refers to the law that impurity from liquids on a vessel's back affects only the back, while impurity on its inside makes the whole vessel impure.

steps.title: What is בית הצביטה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, 'בית הצביטה', and asks what it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'and the בית הצביטה,' and so on. What is בית הצביטה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה's list and asks what the word means. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is only about what the word means. The גמרא needs to know which part of the vessel is called בית הצביטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A special spot on a vessel; its exact meaning is discussed next
Et cetera; the quote from the משנה continues

phrases.english: "And the place of gripping," etc.
What is "the place of gripping"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּית הַצְּבִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from 'back and inside' to the next term in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What part of a vessel is called בית הצביטה?

steps.title: שמואל: the spot where you grip the vessel
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says בית הצביטה is the place where a person grips the vessel. He brings proof from the word 'ויצבט' in רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it is the place where one grips it. And so the פסוק says: 'And he passed her parched grain.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the first definition: בית הצביטה is the spot on the vessel used to grip it. He shows that 'צבט' means taking hold and handing over, using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'ויצבט' describes handing over a small amount, as if taken with the fingers. So בית הצביטה is the part of the vessel you grab with your fingers.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says. It introduces a פסוק that supports the word's meaning.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is the place where one grips it,
and similarly it says:
"And he passed her parched grain."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הצביטה is the spot on a vessel used to grip it, based on the meaning of 'ויצבט' in רות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the spot where neat people dip
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a different definition: בית הצביטה is the small spot on the vessel where careful, neat people dip their food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is the place where fastidious people dip.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion explains the same word differently. רבי יוחנן says it is a small dipping spot attached to the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that בית הצביטה is a separate small part of the vessel. They disagree about what that part is: a grip for holding the vessel, or a little spot for dipping food.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of בית הצביטה: שמואל says it is a grip for holding the vessel, and רבי יוחנן says it is a small spot for dipping food.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is the place where fastidious people dip.
phrases.notes: Here 'צובעין' means dipping food into a little spot on the side of the vessel, not dyeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of Step 22, different from שמואל's answer in Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הצביטה is a small spot attached to the vessel where fastidious people dip their food.

steps.title: רב ביבי's teaching: no back/inside split for any vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי teaches a ברייתא in front of רב נחמן. It says no vessel has the back/inside split, whether the food is קדשי המקדש or קדשי הגבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי taught before רב נחמן: For all vessels there is no difference between back and inside, both for the holy foods of the Temple and for the holy foods outside the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי brings a ברייתא that seems to widen the stricter rule. He says the back and the inside of a vessel are never treated separately, both for Temple holy food and for holy food outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 we learned that for some foods, if only the back of a vessel became impure, only the back is impure. This ברייתא says that for all holy food, both kinds, there is no such split, so the whole vessel is impure. The big question is what 'קדשי הגבול' means here.

keyTerms.meaning: the back (outside) and the inside of a vessel
holy foods of the outlying areas, eaten outside the Temple

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai taught before Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים אֵין לָהֶם אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ,
phrases.english: All vessels do not have a back and inside,
phrases.notes: He means there is no split: if any part of the vessel becomes impure, the whole vessel is impure.

phrases.english: both for the holy foods of the Temple
and for the holy foods of the outlying areas.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the back and inside of a vessel by bringing a ברייתא about how far the rule reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For both קדשי המקדש and קדשי הגבול, a vessel's back and inside are not split; the whole vessel becomes impure.

steps.title: רב נחמן: but the משנה applies the split to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks what קדשי הגבול could mean. If it means תרומה, the משנה clearly says the back/inside split does apply to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What are 'holy foods of outlying areas'? תרומה! But we learned in the משנה: back, inside, and the gripping place apply to תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the ברייתא. The usual meaning of 'קדשי הגבול' is תרומה, but our משנה says תרומה does have the back/inside split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says קדשי הגבול have no split. The משנה says תרומה does have the split. If קדשי הגבול means תרומה, the two sources contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: the gift of produce given to a כהן, eaten even outside the Temple

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קׇדְשֵׁי הַגְּבוּל מַאי נִינְהוּ —
phrases.english: He said to him: The holy foods of outlying areas, what are they?
Terumah!
But didn't we learn: back and inside
and the gripping place apply to terumah!
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה, the lines discussed in steps 20–24.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קׇדְשֵׁי הַגְּבוּל מַאי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 25 from our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that קדשי הגבול have no back/inside split.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קדשי הגבול normally means תרומה, and the משנה says תרומה does have the back/inside split, so the ברייתא contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: Perhaps you mean ordinary food kept at the purity level of holy food
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן offers his own answer. The ברייתא's 'קדשי הגבול' means חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש, not תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you are speaking of ordinary food prepared at the purity level of holy food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן solves his own question. He suggests the ברייתא was talking about ordinary food that people chose to keep at the purity level of קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people outside the Temple guard ordinary food as strictly as קודש, so it can be called 'holy food outside the Temple.' Since this is not תרומה, the ברייתא no longer contradicts the משנה about תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: ordinary food prepared at the purity level of holy food

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'קדשי הגבול' does not mean real holy food. It is ordinary food that is only treated like holy food.

phrases.english: Perhaps about ordinary food
prepared at the purity of holy food you are speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדשי הגבול means תרומה, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: קדשי הגבול means חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש, which is a different category from תרומה, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רבה בר אבוה: six stringencies apply to such ordinary food
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן recalls that רבה בר אבוה said the משנה lists eleven מעלות. The first six apply both to קודש and to חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש. The last five apply only to קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: You reminded me of what רבה בר אבוה said: Eleven stringencies were taught here. The first six apply both to holy food and to ordinary food kept at holy purity. The last ones apply to holy food, but not to ordinary food kept at holy purity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי's ברייתא reminds רב נחמן of a teaching from רבה בר אבוה. That teaching supports the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The back/inside rule is one of the first six מעלות. So רבה בר אבוה agrees that it applies to חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש. This fits the ברייתא read as talking about such חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: you have reminded me of something
stringencies (extra strict rules for holy food)
the first ones / the last ones

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'קדשי הגבול' means חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש. Such food gets the first six מעלות of the משנה, including no back/inside split, but not the last five.

phrases.english: You have reminded me of something
that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Eleven stringencies were taught here;
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our משנה, which lists ways holy food is treated more strictly than תרומה.

phrases.english: the first six apply both to holy food

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and to ordinary food prepared at the purity of holy food;
the last ones apply to holy food,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא לְחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: but not to ordinary food prepared at the purity of holy food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְכַּרְתַּן מִילְּתָא דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier teaching that backs up the answer of step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That חולין שנעשו על טהרת הקודש are treated strictly in some of the משנה's מעלות, such as the back/inside rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר אבוה's statement that the first six of the eleven מעלות apply to such חולין.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sorts the משנה's list into two groups. Only real קודש gets all eleven stringencies.

steps.title: Why may one carrying a מדרס not carry holy food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next rule in the משנה. One carrying a מדרס may carry תרומה but not קודש. Then it asks why קודש is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who carries a מדרס may carry תרומה, but not holy food. Holy food, what is the reason he may not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It asks why carrying קודש together with a מדרס is forbidden when carrying תרומה that way is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he makes sure the impure object never touches the food, there seems to be no reason to forbid it. The גמרא wants to know what makes קודש stricter here.

keyTerms.meaning: an item made impure by a זב sitting or lying on it

phrases.english: One who carries a midras
may carry terumah,
phrases.notes: He means at the same time, as long as nothing impure touches the תרומה.

phrases.english: but not holy food.
Holy food, what is the reason not?

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹדֶשׁ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the back/inside topic and turns to the next מעלה in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason one carrying a מדרס may not carry קודש, when he may carry תרומה.

steps.title: Because of a story that happened, told by שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule was made because of a real event. רב יהודה quotes שמואל, who begins telling about a man moving a barrel of holy wine from place to place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of an incident that happened. As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: There was an incident with someone who was moving a barrel of holy wine from place to place,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this rule was made because of something that once happened. It begins telling that story, which continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not based on pure logic. The חכמים made it because of a real event. Here we only hear the setup: a man carrying a barrel of holy wine. What went wrong comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: because of an incident that happened

phrases.english: Because of an incident that happened.
As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
There was an incident with someone who was moving
a barrel of holy wine
from place to place,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29 by pointing to a historical event.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on carrying קודש with a מדרס comes from a real incident, told by שמואל, involving a barrel of holy wine.
